blocks.text: Wi-Fi security protects the network from unauthorised access. Without it, anyone nearby can use the Internet connection, and hackers can steal personal information from an unsecured network. Securing Wi-Fi keeps data safe and private, and also stops outsiders from using up the connection and slowing it down.

items: Router configuration: the router web interface is opened in a web browser by typing the router's IP address; a username and password are needed to log in. It is used to change the Wi-Fi name and password and to control the security settings.

Wi-Fi encryption: protects data sent over the network by converting it into a secure form. WPA2 and WPA3 are the common security protocols; older ones such as WEP are not secure. Always choose the latest encryption method available.

Default gateway: the device, usually the router, that connects the local network to other networks. Data meant for outside networks goes through the gateway, which forwards it to the correct network; Internet access depends on setting it correctly.

blocks.title: Class activity
blocks.text: Create a sample strong password at least eight characters long, mixing letters and numbers.

blocks.title: Longer passwords are stronger
blocks.text: Eight characters is the book's minimum for the activity. Current guidance prefers longer passwords or passphrases, about 12 characters or more, mixing upper- and lower-case letters, numbers and symbols, and never reusing the router's default password.

A guest network lets visitors use the Internet while keeping them separate from the main home network, so guests cannot reach personal devices. This increases safety and privacy, helps control Internet usage, and is useful in homes and offices.

blocks.prompt: Why should WPA2 or WPA3 be chosen instead of WEP?
blocks.explanation: WEP is an old protocol that is no longer secure; WPA2 and WPA3 use stronger encryption, so data sent over Wi-Fi cannot easily be stolen.
The device (usually the router) through which a local network sends data to other networks such as the Internet.

items: Wi-Fi security stops unauthorised use and data theft.
Router web interface: change the Wi-Fi name, password and security settings.
Use WPA2/WPA3, not WEP; the router is the default gateway; give visitors a guest network.
